Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
As we get back to business after the festive period may I wish 
you a very Happy New Year - I hope you had a very enjoyable 
Christmas break and took the opportunity to recharge and 
reflect after a very busy year. To usher in the New Year, a 
spectacular fireworks display took place in Howth Harbour to 
co-ordinate with another showcase at Dún Laoghaire Harbour. 
The free, family friendly event was held in collaboration with 
New Year’s Festival Dublin as part of the wider ‘Winter in 
Dublin Programme’ which aims to boost tourism and create 
economic opportunities in the county in the winter season. 
Last year saw the first New Years Eve fireworks show take 
place and I am very pleased that this year’s extravaganza was 
also incredibly successful with many thousands of spectators 
gathering for the Fingal display in Howth. I have no doubt that 
this festival of celebration will go from strength to strength 
each year and will be a much-anticipated annual event in 
Fingal.  
A variation to the Fingal Development Plan 2023-2029 was 
published on December 23, 2025, and will be on public display 
until January 29, 2026. The proposal seeks to unlock additional 
residential zoning to provide for an extra 5,000 homes in 
response to the recently published National Housing 
Guidelines. This proposed variation was prompted by the 
publication of the new guidelines in July, following which, the 
Minister for Housing, James Browne TD, asked all 31 local 
authorities to review their Development Plans and incorporate 
the new annual housing delivery targets. The Council’s 
planning team immediately commenced the process of 
reviewing residential zoned lands across the county whereby 
lands both within and outside existing settlements and urban 
areas were examined in the context of identifying potential 
sites for development. The current Development Plan, when 
adopted in 2023 by the Elected Members, outlined the plan to 
deliver 35,000 new homes – 7,000 of these homes have already 
been provided and the variation seeks to increase the delivery 
of new homes by an additional 5,000. This increase 
demonstrates Fingal’s commitment to providing high quality, 
compact and energy efficient homes while simultaneously 
forging new communities which are centred around transport 
links thus reducing the need for car-dependant growth. The 
variation will be on public display until January 29, 2026, and 
supporting 
documents 
can 
be 
viewed 
at https://consult.fingal.ie where 
submissions 
and 
observations on the proposal can also be made.  
I am pleased that Fingal County Council’s Gaeltacht 
Scholarship Scheme is open for applications for this coming 
year offering Partial Scholarships of €500 to Fingal Second 
Level students who are attending residential Gaeltacht Irish 
Language Courses in 2026. The scheme, which commenced in 
2024, has attracted huge interest from families of students 
who will be heading to Gaeltacht areas during the year to focus 
on honing their Irish language skills. These trips not only give 
students the opportunity to improve their Irish but also 
provide a valuable social and cultural focus which instils a love 
for the Irish language and heritage.  
This year, 15 lucky students will receive scholarships and will 
be invited to the Seachtain na Gaeilge event in County Hall 
Swords to meet Mayor of Fingal Cllr Tom O'Leary and to take 
part in a photocall. Interested parties can find out more about 
this initiative here: https://www.fingal.ie/gaeltacht - Go n-éirí 
libh! As always, Seachtain na Gaeilge will be taking place from 
March 1 – 17 and Fingal County Council’s programme of events 
promises a true celebration of the language and culture. Our 
library branches have fantastic events on offer including 
Family Yoga, Magic and Puppet Shows and Bilingual Story 
Telling to name but a few offerings. One of the highlights each 
year is the Ceol, Craic agus Gaeilge event at County Hall where 
you can be sure of a wonderfully entertaining evening with live 
music, chats and a great atmosphere. Full details on the event 
are here https://www.fingal.ie/ga/ga/SeachtainnaGaeilge2025 
whether you use the Irish language every day or simply wish 
to improve your cúpla focal, you are more than welcome to 
join us on Wednesday March 11, 2026, at 7pm. 
This month will see a number of changes introduced to the 
organisation as a response to the challenges posed by the 
continuing growth of population within the county. Fingal 
County Council is committed to the delivery of housing, key 
infrastructure projects and excellent standards of efficiency 
and co-ordination in our work – these objectives will be greatly 
assisted by the appointment of a new Director of Service and 
the 
creation 
of 
standalone 
Housing, 
Planning, 
and 
Infrastructure directorates. I am pleased that Senior Planner 
Róisín Burke has been appointed as Director of Planning and 
Development and will head up a directorate that will lead on 
planning 
policy, 
development 
management, 
and 
the 
identification of land activation priorities and infrastructure 
obstacles. Róisín brings to the position a wealth of experience 
and knowledge accumulated through her work with other local 
authorities and Fingal County Council which she joined in 
2008. I know you will join me in wishing Róisín the very best as 
she embarks on her new role. The current Director of Planning 
and Strategic Infrastructure, Matthew McAleese, will lead a 
dedicated Infrastructure and Transport Directorate and Paul 
Carroll, who is Director of Housing and Community 
Development at present, will oversee a dedicated Housing 
Department. The Economic, Enterprise, Tourism and Cultural 
Development Department will now assume responsibility for 
the Community Development Department aligning it more 
closely with the Local Economic and Community Development 
Committee. Through these important changes, I look forward 
to building on Fingal County Council’s solid record of service 
delivery for the future. 
 
Best wishes, 
      
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
 
New Destination Brand for Tourism  
The upcoming launch of Fingal’s new destination 
brand on 23rd February represents a key milestone in 
the implementation of the Fingal Tourism Strategy. It 
will include a brand identity, website, and social 
media rollout as well as a comprehensive Marketing 
& PR Programme. 
This event which will be held in the Grand Hotel, 
Malahide brings together tourism, hospitality, and 
wider industry partners to align, collaborate, and 
activate the next phase of Fingal’s destination 
growth. 
It 
strongly 
reinforces 
the 
Council’s 
commitment to developing a competitive, high-
performing tourism offering centred around the new 
brand. The launch will be a starting point for 
engaging media, stakeholders and the wider 
community. 
 
Winter in Dublin  
Fingal is once again participating in the Winter in 
Dublin (WID) programme which is designed to 
support the capital’s tourism sector by encouraging 
domestic and international visitors outside the 
traditional peak seasons.  
Page 4 
Such strategic initiatives are central to Fáilte Ireland’s 
work in driving seasonal and regional spread and in 
building 
a 
more 
resilient, 
year-round 
visitor 
economy.  Winter in Dublin is run by Visit Dublin and 
is a collaborative event between Fáilte Ireland and 
Dublin stakeholders including local authorities, 
public bodies, representative organisations, and 
industry partners. 
WID in Fingal includes Wonderlights at Malahide 
Castle and the fireworks at Howth Harbour which will 
be a centrepiece of the celebrations on New Years 
Eve.  
 
 
 
TradFest 2026  
 
 
 
Over 30 concerts will take place across Fingal as part 
of TradFest 2026 running from 21-25 January 2026. 
TradFest is a joyful celebration of Irish music and 
culture all over Dublin City and County. 
Fingal venues include Ardgillan Castle, Malahide 
Castle, Swords Castle Chapel, The Millbank Theatre, 
Draíocht Theatre, The Abbey Tavern and The Séamus 
Ennis Arts Centre as well as exciting new locations 
such as The Little Theatre in Skerries, Saint Macullin 
Community Centre in Lusk, and the Lusk Cultural 
Centre.

A key part of TradFest 2026, is Féile Barney 
celebrating the life and career of the legendary 
Barney McKenna of The Dubliners, over a three-day 
festival in Howth, the seaside town he called 
home. TradFest also will deliver an expanded 
community programme later this year which will 
outline a series of new exciting, free community-led 
events in Fingal.

56% heard about the market via social media 
80% of people rated it good to excellent

Youth & Education  
 
Fingal Arts Office is delighted to announce that artist 
Órla Kelly has been awarded the Fingal Exploring & 
Thinking Bursary Award 2025/2026. 
Exploring and Thinking is a collaborative framework 
for early childhood arts in the Dublin region, 
developed by the four Dublin local authorities. It is a 
significant recognition for artists working in early 
childhood arts. It provides artists with valuable time, 
resources, and space to reflect on and deepen their 
practice. One bursary has been granted per 
participating local authority involved - artist Órla Kelly 
(Fingal), David Beattie (Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown), 
Michelle Henry (South Dublin), and Jane Hackett 
(Dublin City), highlighting their innovative practices 
and commitment to creating work with and for 
marginalised children.

Swords Cultural Quarter 
On December 2nd the Arts Office hosted a closed 
enquiry consultation session with industry leaders 
which sought to explore what Fingal County Council 
and the Arts Office need to put in place now to 
ensure Culture House is ready to support artists and 
engage audiences successfully. Participants strongly 
affirmed the potential of SCQ and Culture House as a 
civic, accessible cultural hub for Swords, stressing the 
need to clearly define its purpose, identity and values 
from the outset. Long-term success was seen to 
depend on an artist-led vision, sustained public 
investment, 
early 
and 
ongoing 
community 
engagement, and a collaborative culture across arts 
and library teams.  
Consultation is ongoing with more sessions planned 
with arts resource organisations, individual artists 
and communities in Q1 2026. 
 
Draíocht

were officially opened in May 2001 by President Mary 
McAleese.  The Arts Centre had opened to the public 
in February 2001, prior to the official launch date, 
with a full visual arts and performance programme.   
Several events are being planned to mark the 
occasion of our 25th birthday.    This includes ‘25!’  An 
Exhibition of works by recent graduates (past 4 years) 
and/or early career artists who are from and/or 
live/work in Fingal.   This is an Open call Exhibition 
with applicants submitting to us by 31st December 
2025.  The selection panel includes Fingal’s County 
Arts Officer, Sarah O’Neill and Fingal artist, Rich 
Gilligan.   All artists selected to exhibit, will be paid a 
fee.  Given Draíocht’s stated commitment to high 
quality arts provision for children and young people, 
we are delighted to engage Helen O’Donoghue 
(previously Head of Education in IMMA) to curate an 
Exhibition for children in 2026, 2027 and 2028.

After an application process, Lucy Hill has been 
awarded the 2026 commission.

Theatre (Ireland) and the subsequent project, ‘NEST’ 
in 2024.

Libraries 
 
Skerries Library Re-opens 
 
 
 
 
 
Fingal Libraries is delighted to welcome the re-
opening of Skerries Library, which has been 
significantly redeveloped, extended, and restored. 
The Mayor of Fingal Cllr. Tom O’Leary will officially 
launch the refurbished library on 29th January. The 
launch will feature the Fanzini street performers, 
Bohemian Strings string quartet, crafts in the 
Creative Zone and author visits from children’s 
authors Alan Nolan, Shane Hegarty and Niamh 
Sharkey.  
Page 10 
With its new, light-filled three-story extension, its 
lecture and meeting rooms, Creative Zone, public PCs 
and printing facilities, 3D printer, ample study space 
and diverse range of stock, the library is equipped to 
serve the Skerries community into the future. A 
programme of classes, workshops and talks for all 
ages has been scheduled throughout the spring to 
celebrate the reopening of the library. In addition, 
there will be an extensive programme of events for 
local schools and a series of workshops for Prosper 
Fingal. The re-opening of Skerries Library marks a 
new chapter in the history of this much-loved 
Carnegie Library. 
 
Donabate Library Moves to Ballisk House 
 
 
 
This January, Donabate Library will move from its 
former location in the community and leisure centre 
to its new premises in Ballisk House on the Portrane 
Road. The Mayor of Fingal Cllr. Tom O’Leary will 
officially launch the new library on 22nd January. The 
launch will feature the Fanzini street performers, 
Bohemian Strings string quartet, and a magic show 
from Reuben the Entertainer for local schoolchildren 
to enjoy. The new library has a meeting room which 
will facilitate events, classes and workshops for all 
ages. Fingal Libraries looks forward to welcoming the 
community to this space for learning, creativity, and 
connection. 
 
Spring Programme of Events at Fingal Libraries 
The brochure outlining the spring 2026 programme 
of events in libraries will be available in library 
branches and on the Fingal Libraries website in 
January.

The programme runs from January to April and 
features a wide range of events, workshops and 
courses for people of all ages supporting literacy, 
health, culture and creativity, the Irish language, 
heritage, STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering,
